about: The standing, special and select committees of the U.S. House and Senate in the 119th Congress (2025-2026), each with its subcommittees as the chambers list them, so a member of Congress can hold real committee and subcommittee seats. Read by src/core2/office-day-federal.ts. The legislature engine refers a bill to one of three subject committees (finance, labor, general); each real committee names the one it stands for in engineCommittee, and lists the starting-law policy question keys its jurisdiction covers. Subcommittee lists come from the chambers' committee index pages as fetched on the retrieval date; the 11 House committees whose Clerk index showed a 'more' link were checked against their own committee sites on the same date (one subcommittee, House Transportation and Infrastructure Oversight and Investigations, was added; task forces listed on the Financial Services, Homeland Security and Oversight sites are not subcommittees and are left out). Each subcommittee's questions list names the policy question keys its jurisdiction covers. Joint committees are not included.
